entries.claim: Primary resources (Field resources) are the resources from which we originally get data through interviewing or questionnaires (survey). This type is distinguished by accuracy, but it needs time and effort and is highly expensive to conduct.
entries.quote: Primary resources (Field resources):
entries.note: Definition stated under '① Primary resources (Field resources):' — text shows these are resources obtained through interviewing or questionnaires, distinguished by accuracy, needs time and efforts, and is highly expensive to conduct

entries.claim: Secondary resources (historical resources): we can get data from authorities and agencies that formally work, such as the central agency for mobilization and statistics, internet and media. This type is a good type of resource because it saves time and money.
entries.quote: Secondary resources (historical resources):
entries.note: Definition stated under '② Secondary resources (historical resources):' — text shows data from authorities/agencies like central agency for mobilization and statistics, internet and media, saves time and money

entries.claim: Method of mass population means collecting the data related to the phenomenon of the statistical society. It is used to include all the society, such as the population. It includes all the values and is unbiased, and the outcomes are very accurate.
entries.quote: It means to collect the data related to the phenomenon
entries.note: Definition stated under 'First : Method of mass population :' — text shows it means to collect data related to phenomenon of statistical society, includes all society/values, is unbiased, and outcomes are accurate

entries.claim: Advantage 1: using samples saves time, efforts and money.
entries.quote: It saves time, efforts and money.

entries.claim: Advantage 2: it is the only way to collect data about gigantic societies (like fish).
entries.quote: The only way to collect data about gigantic societies (like fish).

entries.claim: Advantage 3: it is the only method to study some limited societies, such as the two cases below.
entries.quote: The only method to study some limited societies such as:

entries.claim: A: Check the patient's blood by getting a sample (checking the whole blood leads to death).
entries.quote: Check the patient blood by getting a sample

entries.claim: B: Check the production of a factory producing electric lamps to determine the validity of the lamp (know for how long the lamp can be used before getting burned).
entries.quote: Check the production of a factory producing electric lamps

entries.claim: A disadvantage of sample methods: outcomes are not accurate if the selected sample doesn't represent all the society well; in such a case the sample is called biased.
entries.quote: the sample is called biased.

entries.claim: Biased selection means selecting the sample in a way to satisfy the objectives of the research; this is called a deliberate sample.
entries.quote: we select the sample in a way to satisfy the objectives

entries.claim: Random selection means selecting a sample such that the chance of getting any value from the society is equal.
entries.quote: the chance of getting any value from the society is equal

entries.claim: 1. Simple random sample: the simplest type of sample; it can be got from homogeneous societies where selection is related to the size and number of units in the society.
entries.quote: Simple random sample: Is the simplest type of samples

entries.claim: A. If the size of the society is small: when choosing 5 students of a 40-student class, prepare an identical card for each student with name or number, put them in a box, draw a card randomly and return it again; repeat until the sample needed is obtained.
entries.quote: If the size of the society is small:

entries.claim: If the size of the society is big (e.g. selecting a sample of 5 students from 800): number the students from 1 to 800, then use the calculator or Excel to give 10 random digits in the field from 0.000 to 0.999, remove the decimal point so the field runs from zero to 999, and discard the digits that are more than 800.
entries.quote: If the size of the society is big:
entries.note: Method for selecting sample from large population (800 students) is stated in section B with matching steps: number students 1-800, use calculator/Excel for 10 random digits in 0.000-0.999, remove decimal to get 0-999 range, discard digits over 800.

entries.claim: Five non-repeated digits are enough to give the numbers of the sample of students.
entries.quote: 5 digits unrepreated are enough to give the digits
entries.note: Text in section 2 directly states '5 digits unrepeated are enough to give the digits of the sample for the students' which matches the claim's rule.

entries.claim: When the society to be examined is heterogeneous or made up of qualitative sets that differ in characteristics, it is divided into homogeneous sets according to the characteristics forming it. Each set is called a layer, and the researcher selects a random sample in which each layer is represented according to its size in the society. Such a sample is called the layer sample.
entries.quote: Layer random sample:
entries.note: Definition of layer random sample under the heading matches the claim's definition with minor wording variations (e.g., 'are different' vs 'differ', 'which' vs 'in which') but same meaning preserved.
